cards.title: Stop AI from Making Stuff Up: The Untapped Goldmine in Fresh Data for Code Assistants
cards.thesis: Developers are increasingly using AI for tasks like code review, but these tools often 'hallucinate' (make up incorrect information) or give outdated advice. This problem is exacerbated by AI models potentially referencing 'obsolete code' found in repositories, leading to frustrating errors and wasted development time.

evidence.text: Many developers are finding AI tools like Claude's /review and /code-review to be incredibly valuable and even more thorough than human code reviewers.
It's a common understanding that all AI can, and will, hallucinate (make up incorrect information).
GitHub and other code repositories contain over 10% obsolete code that no one ever deletes, costing money to store.
DeepSeek's new pricing shows a significant difference, with peak hours costing twice as much as off-peak, highlighting the need to optimize AI model usage.

cards.opportunity: The biggest pain point right now for anyone building with AI code assistants is when they 'hallucinate' (make things up) or suggest outdated solutions. Instead of letting your AI tool pull from stale public data or old project code, build a lightweight plug-in that feeds it *only* the most current, relevant documentation from your internal wikis, recent code changes, or even a scraper for live API docs. This isn't just about accuracy; it's about making your AI faster, more reliable, and ultimately cheaper by reducing wasted 'thinking' on bad information, and you could ship a basic version in a weekend.

cards.title: Escape the Info Avalanche: Your Digital Assets Need a Home
cards.thesis: People are overwhelmed by the sheer volume of online content, especially with AI, and simultaneously struggling to find reliable places to store and share their own digital creations. Existing solutions for both information digestion and personal archiving are proving unreliable or insufficient, leaving a clear need for tools that offer trusted, personalized content management.

evidence.text: People are finding it harder to keep up with interesting articles on Hacker News, especially in the last 2-3 years because of AI, and are wondering how to deal with the overload without just ignoring everything.

A musician with over 300 albums needs an alternative to the Internet Archive for storing their music, as the service has become unreliable for uploads after a 2024 attack, causing frustration when trying to meet specific release dates.
The project XIAZY/wcctl is a command-line tool designed to connect WeChat with other tools, indicating a need to bridge popular but often closed platforms with other services.

cards.opportunity: While everyone's drowning in AI-generated noise and major archives like the Internet Archive are failing creators, there's a wide-open lane for a 'personal digital trust layer.' Forget just filtering news; the real gap is a simple, reliable service that acts as *your* guaranteed personal vault for digital creations (think a musician's albums with specific release dates) that *also* intelligently curates external information relevant to *your* stored content. You could launch a basic version this weekend offering rock-solid file archiving with immutable timestamps, then layer on AI-powered content discovery that learns from what you've archived.
